criteria.text: Per-profile (or per-task-kind) tier policy — e.g. secretary triage -> haiku-class, planning -> opus-class; explicit override wins.
criteria.test_id: issue-844-c1: resolveModelTier maps known task kinds to the correct tier (triage/formatting/extraction/summarization -> cheap, planning/judgment -> frontier); an explicit modelOverride / profile model_tier_hint always wins over the task-kind default

criteria.text: Budget awareness — near budget, the resolver prefers cheaper tiers AND surfaces that it did.
criteria.test_id: issue-844-c2: when usage_budget_service reports a provider's remaining budget below the near-budget threshold, resolveTieredModel downgrades the chosen route to a cheaper tier and sets downgradedForBudget:true with a reason string on the returned decision; when budget is healthy the requested tier is honored and downgradedForBudget is false

criteria.text: Decisions logged (model chosen + why) so the org audit (#819) can measure cost per outcome — one structured log line, no payloads.
criteria.test_id: issue-844-c3: resolveTieredModel emits exactly one logger.info call per decision with a JSON-parseable payload containing provider, modelID, tier, taskKind, reason, downgradedForBudget, and overrideApplied fields; the logged payload never contains a 'prompt', 'text', or 'messages' key (no payload leakage)

criteria.text: Explicit user override ALWAYS wins over both tier policy and budget-based downgrade.
criteria.test_id: issue-844-c4: when an explicit modelOverride is supplied, resolveTieredModel returns it unchanged even when the profile/task-kind policy would pick a different tier AND even when the budget is critically low (overrideApplied:true, downgradedForBudget:false)
